Today I thought I'd talk about some of the reasons you might choose bodyweight fitness even though you have the means to access barbells without any inconvenience. I myself am among this class [there's a Gold's right down the road and membership is only $30/month, thanks lazy people who sign up and then never go thus subsidizing it for the rest of us], so I decided to share some insights.

Reason number one anyone will give you to do bodyweight is, of course, that you don't need weights, or really very much equipment at all. I realize that this is the deciding factor for most people who come to this sub. They just don't have the means to get to the iron. If you're one of them, consider this list a way to make yourself feel better about your decision to take up bodyweight. If you're not among them, consider this list a way to make you either change your mind and make the switch [or at least include some bodyweight moves in your routine], or further confirm your own beliefs. So without further ado, here are some of the advantages [yes, advantages] of bodyweight over barbells.

Number one in my book is the dramatically reduced risk of injury. You can't make a mistake and cut your head off with a pushup variation, and you can't actually crush your skull doing bodyweight skullcrushers. This doesn't just apply to acute injuries, however, as chronic injuries should also be reduced, due to the closed kinetic chain nature of nearly all bodyweight exercises, and the lack of an external load adding stress to the joints. I, for one, know that my joints hurt far more after I do a weights session than they ever have with even the most intense bodyweight session.

Second might be how with bodyweight you can continue to progress on a cut, due to the fact that the load is decreasing as your bodyweight does. This might not seem like a huge deal to the inexperienced, but it's psychologically amazing to be able to actually progress while cutting weight rather than just stagnating, or even worse, losing strength, like you would with barbells. Why give yourself a reason to give up halfway through a cut if you don't have to? Bodyweight simply encourages leanness rather than bulk, espiecially to those who want to master more advanced movements.

Continuing along the same path, bodyweight gives you variety, and a continuous stream of new things to master, over years and years of training. Doing the same movements over and over again, year after year gets boring, at least to most people. With both bodyweight and weights you are constantly improving, but with bodyweight these improvements come in the form of newer, more exciting and more impressive exercises for you to learn and master. This can continue for years per progression, before you eventually hit a "master step" type exercise that you'll never do with perfect form for more than a few reps [like one-arm pullups]. Even then, though, you can always switch to a different progression or find some other new way to mix things up.

Then there's the convenience factor. Sure, maybe you can get access to a gym, but it's still inconvenient to take time out of your day to travel all the way there and back, and it's small stuff like that that often keeps people from ever working out in the first place. Maybe you think you have an iron will, but why take the risk that you might slack off if you don't have to? With bodyweight you can work out right in your home, with zero travel time, and heck, you can even accomplish other stuff between sets if you want.

Finally, there's the fact that bodyweight movements work and improve other athletic attributes besides strength, such as balance and flexibility. A good pistol squat, for example, requires a lot of both of these. Also, full body movements like muscle-ups, common in bodyweight training, teach you to use your entire body as a unit, unlike some exercises which isolate muscle groups.

So, fellow people who do bodyweight out of choice rather than necessity, why do you do it? Have I missed anything important? Post your thoughts below.

While I got into bodyweight training out of necessity I think I'd keep doing it even if I had access to a gym. All the cool bodyweight motivational training videos with people doing muscle ups, planches (sp?), front/back levers, just look amazing.
